ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Orthopedics & Sports Medicine
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
She presents to the clinic with a 3-month history of a painless swelling on the back of her left wrist.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
She reports that the swelling fluctuates in size and becomes more prominent when she flexes her wrist. She denies any trauma to the area, weakness, or numbness in her hand.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Her medical history is unremarkable

MEDICATIONS:
She takes no medications.

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- No significant family history

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Social (1-2 drinks per month). Occupation: Software developer.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, there is a 2 cm, round, firm, mobile mass on the dorsal surface of the wrist. The mass transilluminates with a penlight. There is no overlying skin change, and the range of motion of the wrist is preserved. The patient's neurovascular examination is normal.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-04-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Orthopedics & Sports Medicine
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
A lump on her wrist that has been growing slowly over the past six months

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient presents for follow-up care three months following her initial outpatient visit for left wrist swelling. She denies any trauma to the area but mentions that the lump becomes more noticeable when she types for extended periods. She reports minimal discomfort but is concerned about the cosmetic appearance.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Ganglion cyst of wrist (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

MEDICATIONS:
She takes no medications

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- No significant family history

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Social (1-2 drinks per month). Occupation: Software developer.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, you note a 2 cm, round, rubbery nodule on the dorsal aspect of her wrist. It is mobile and does not appear to be attached to the underlying structures. The overlying skin is intact and non-erythematous. Light transmission through the nodule is positive upon transillumination. There is no limitation of movement, and the strength of the wrist is preserved.
